solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S026-01.notes: Praise plus a limited trial is approval with reservations, so 'qualified' fits. Students who only know the 'competent' sense of 'qualified' may choose 'enthusiastic' because of the praise.

S026-02.notes: Hammered into a thin sheet without tearing means malleable. The fact checks out: about 1 m² per gram matches the usual 'one ounce covers about 300 sq ft' figure.

flags: minor: 'Studies of species and their histories' is vague wording; e.g., 'genetic and historical studies' would read more naturally
S026-03.notes: The text gives an assumption, then the evidence against it, then current research. The facts are accurate: glaciation largely wiped out native earthworms there, and the current ones came from Europe and Asia.

flags: minor: choice D contains its own justification ('since trees with a steady water supply grew normally'), which makes it stand out from the other choices
S026-04.notes: Only the trees without steady groundwater were affected, which points to drought. A is ruled out by 'every tree', B by the wrong location, and C has no support in the text.

S026-05.notes: Harvest per plot is 2000/40=50, 1500/25=60 and 1050/15=70. Only B compares output per plot.

S026-06.notes: A participial phrase in apposition needs no finite verb. A, B and D each create a second main verb or clause and leave the sentence ungrammatical.

S026-07.notes: The singular subject is the novel, so the verb is 'tells'. The plural-looking title 'The Orchards' is the trap; present tense fits a description of a literary work.

S026-08.notes: The experiment is an example supporting the claim. This matches real research (Appel & Cocroft 2014, Arabidopsis/thale cress).

S026-09.notes: Only C gives the habitat and the range.

flags: minor: the claim has two parts (the wind cannot be seen; it is known by its effects). D directly shows the first part, so some students will pick D. B is best because its 'But when...' covers the effects part, which is the claim's distinctive point and which no other choice addresses.
S026-10.notes: The quoted lines are accurate (stanza 1 of Rossetti's poem in Sing-Song, dated 1872). B shows the wind known through the trembling leaves. A, C and D only say that no one sees the wind.
